dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:2601.text: The bladder, 𦜶光. From 肉; 孚 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2602.text: The large and small intestines. From 肉; 昜 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2603.text: Fat. From 肉; 高 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2604.text: Fat. From 肉; 方 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2605.text: The chest. From 肉; 𤸰 supplies the sound. [The recorded headword 钋 does not match the described formation.]

shuowen:2606.text: The breastbone. From 肉; 乙 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2607.text: The back or spine. From 肉; 北 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2608.text: The two flanks. From 肉; 劦 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2609.text: The flank. From 肉; 㫄 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2610.text: Flank flesh. From 肉; 寽 supplies the sound. Another explanation: fat between the intestines; another: 膫.

shuowen:2611.text: The rib bones. From 肉; 力 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2612.text: Flesh flanking the spine. From 肉; 申 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2613.text: Back flesh. From 肉; 𣫭 supplies the sound. The Changes says: “Affecting the back flesh.”

shuowen:2615.text: Beneath the armpit. From 肉; 各 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2616.text: Beneath the armpit. From 肉; 去 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2617.text: The part above the hand, the arm. From 肉; 辟 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2618.text: The arm's 羊矢 bone, apparently the upper arm. From 肉; 需 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 襦. [The anatomical phrase is uncertain.]

shuowen:2619.text: The joint of the arm. From 肉 and 寸; 寸 is the hand's pulse point.

shuowen:2620.text: The navel, 𦚚𪗇. From 肉; 齊 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2621.text: Thick. From 肉; 复 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2622.text: Fat below the abdomen. From 肉; 臾 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2623.text: The buttocks. From 肉; 隹 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2624.text: An opening. From 肉; abbreviated 決 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 決 in “letting water flow.”

shuowen:2625.text: The thigh. From 肉; 夸 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2626.text: The thigh. From 肉; 殳 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2627.text: The shank. From 肉; 卻 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2628.text: The shank, 胻. From 肉; 坙 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2629.text: The end of the shank. From 肉; 行 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2630.text: The calf of the leg. From 肉; 非 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2631.text: The calf muscle. From 肉; 耑 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2632.text: The body's four limbs. From 肉; 只 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2633.text: Hair on the big toe. From 肉; 亥 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2634.text: Resemblance among blood kin. From 肉; 小 supplies the sound. Not resembling one's forebears is therefore called 不肖.

shuowen:2635.text: Descendants continuing one another in succession. From 肉; 八 depicts growing, and 幺 depicts successive layers.

shuowen:2636.text: Descendants. From 肉; 由 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2637.text: Shaking or vibration. From 肉; 八 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2638.text: Flesh bare or exposed. From 肉; 亶 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “Baring the chest to fight a tiger.”

shuowen:2639.text: A rustic Yizhou term for a large person: avoiding saying “fat,” they call the person 䑋. From 肉; 襄 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2640.text: Emaciated. From 肉; 皆 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2641.text: Having little flesh. From 肉; 瞿 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2642.text: Losing flesh and becoming thin. From 肉; 兌 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2643.text: People of Qi call emaciation 脙. From 肉; 求 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 休 in 休止.

shuowen:2644.text: Emaciated. From 肉; 䜌 supplies the sound. Another explanation: cut meat, 臠. The Odes says: “The distressed person is wasted away.”

shuowen:2645.text: Thin. From 肉; 𦟝 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2646.text: Foolish. From 肉; 丞 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 丞.

shuowen:2647.text: A sore on the lips. From 肉; 㐱 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2648.text: A scar or callus. From 肉; 垂 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2649.text: A callus, 腄. From 肉; 氐 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2650.text: An excrescence. From 肉; 尤 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2651.text: A sore arising from scratching. From 肉; 丸 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2652.text: An abscess. From 肉; 重 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2653.text: A displaced bone. From 肉; 失 supplies the sound. Pronounced the same as 跌.

shuowen:2654.text: Flesh turning outward from a wound. From 肉; 希 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2655.text: A scar. From 肉; 引 supplies the sound. Another explanation: sudden or urgent, 遽. [The alternate gloss is uncertain.]

shuowen:2656.text: On the third xu day after the winter solstice, the 臘 sacrifice is made to the hundred spirits. From 肉; 巤 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2657.text: A Chu custom of sacrificing and feasting in the second month. From 肉; 婁 supplies the sound. Another explanation: praying for grain and eating the new crop is called 離膢.

shuowen:2658.text: A sacrifice. From 肉; 兆 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2659.text: Blessed meat from a sacrifice. From 肉; 乍 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2660.text: To split flesh. From 肉 and abbreviated 隓.

shuowen:2661.text: To provide food. From 肉; 善 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2662.text: Fine, good meat. From 肉; 柔 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2663.text: To eat. From 肉; 爻 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2664.text: To set out food abundantly, 腆腆. From 肉; 典 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2665.text: Of cattle and sheep, fat is called 𦘺; of pigs, 腯. From 肉; 盾 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2666.text: Fat meat. From 肉; 必 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2667.text: The flesh hanging from a cow's neck. From 肉; 古 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2668.text: An ox's manyfold stomach. From 肉; abbreviated 弦 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2669.text: An ox's manyfold stomach. From 肉; 𣬉 supplies the sound. Another explanation: a bird's gizzard, 膍胵.

shuowen:2670.text: A bird's stomach. From 肉; 至 supplies the sound. Another explanation: 胵 is the collective name for the five organs.

shuowen:2671.text: Flesh adjoining the hide behind an ox's flank and in front of its thigh. From 肉; 𤐫 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 繇.

shuowen:2672.text: Meat for a blood sacrifice. From 肉; 帥 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2673.text: Fat around an ox's intestines. From 肉; 尞 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “Take its blood and intestinal fat.”

shuowen:2674.text: Dried meat. From 肉; 甫 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2675.text: Dried meat. From 肉; 攸 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2676.text: Dried meat. From 肉; 奚 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2677.text: Dried meat, 膎. From 肉; 兩 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2678.text: Thin dried meat, spread on the roof. From 肉; 尃 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2679.text: The stomach repository. From 肉; 完 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 患. Older wording says “dried meat.”

shuowen:2680.text: A strip of dried meat. From 肉; 句 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2681.text: Boneless dried meat. Yang Xiong explains: dried bird meat. From 肉; 無 supplies the sound. The Rites of Zhou has 膴判. Pronounced like 謨.

shuowen:2682.text: Crab paste. From 肉; 疋 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2683.text: In the north, dried bird meat is called 腒. From 肉; 居 supplies the sound. A tradition says: “Yao was like dried beast meat; Shun like dried bird meat.”

shuowen:2684.text: Sauce made from cooked meat. From 肉; 九 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 舊.

shuowen:2685.text: Dried fish with tails described as 䐹䐹. From 肉; 肅 supplies the sound. The Rites of Zhou has “腒䐹.” [The exact tail description is uncertain.]

shuowen:2686.text: Meat paste containing bone. From 肉; 耎 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2687.text: Raw meat sauce. From 肉; 延 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2688.text: Pork sauce. From 肉; 否 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2689.text: Cooked until soft. From 肉; 而 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2690.text: To cut cooked meat and mix it into blood. From 肉; 員 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 遜.

shuowen:2691.text: The smell of dog fat. From 肉; 生 supplies the sound. Another explanation: uncooked.

shuowen:2692.text: The smell of pig fat. From 肉; 喿 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2693.text: Pork soup. From 肉; 堯 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2694.text: Feeding pigs when stars appear causes small fleshy growths to form in their meat. From 肉 and 星; 星 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2695.text: In horned animals it is called 脂; in hornless ones, 膏. From 肉; 旨 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2696.text: The action or material 觷, perhaps working hard tissue. From 肉; 𧴪 supplies the sound. [The rare cross-gloss is unresolved.]

shuowen:2697.text: Fat on the surface. From 肉; 貳 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2698.text: Membranes between flesh. From 肉; 莫 supplies the sound. [The anatomical expression 胲膜 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2699.text: That outside the flesh but inside the skin. From 肉; 弱 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2700.text: Meat soup. From 肉; 隺 supplies the sound.
